newsitem.title: USA: Riggs seen among takeover targets - report.
newsitem.headline: Riggs seen among takeover targets - report.

text.p: Riggs National Corp, California Financial Holding Co, and Summit Bancorp could be upcoming targets for takeovers in the U.S. banking industry, Barron's financial weekly said.
The newspaper cited Jim Schmidt, manager of the John Hancock Regional Bank fund, saying he focuses on buying medium-sized bank stocks that are potential takeover targets.
"Who's next? If I had to guess, I'd say Riggs National, California Financial and Summit Bancorp," Schmidt was quoted as saying in Barron's September 9 issue.
Schmidt viewed Boatmen's Bancshares Inc as a potential takeover target and made it one of his fund's largest holdings ahead of NationsBank Corp's recent bid for the bank.

His fund's largest holdings include H.F. Ahmanson and Co, AmSouth Bancorp, Bank of New York Co Inc, First American Corp, First of America Bank Corp, Hibernia Corp, Long Island Bancorp Inc, Union Planters Corp, and U.S. Bancorp, the newspaper said.
Schmidt also likes Compass Bancshares Inc and First Commerce Corp, Barron's said.
Schmidt said the United States has gone from having 14,000 banks to 10,000 in the past 10 years and is on its way to 4,000 within the next 15 years.
"By the year 2000, you could have 15 huge banks with most of the assets, alongside several thousand tiny banks. The highest mortality will be among middle-sized banks," he told the newspaper.
